newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg-Dillon merger unites blue-chip clients.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg-Dillon merger unites blue-chip clients.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp's $600 million takeover of privately-owned Dillon Read & Co announced on Thursday unites two sets of high-quality clients.
Both U.S. investment bank Dillon Read and London-based SBC Warburg enjoy lists of blue-chip clients and compete for high-quality mandates for equity offerings.
Warburg, credited among other things with creating the Eurobond market, was bought by SBC in 1995 after a proposed merger with Morgan Stanley foundered.
The following is a summary of some recent deals involving the firms.
DILLON READ:
Advises on $10.5 billion merger of Kimberley-Clark with
Scott Paper
Advises on $4.3 billion recapitalisation of Levi Strauss & Co
Advises on $13.1 billion sale of Rockwell International
aerospace division to Boeing Co
Advises on Rockwell $1.6 billion spinoff of automotive unit.
SBC WARBURG:
Advises Grand Metropolitan Plc in merger with Guinness
Plc to create 24-billion-pound company.
Advises Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in $8 billion
purchase of speciality chemicals businesses from Unilever.
Awarded mandate by Italy for privatisation of motorway group
Autostrade, by coincidence the first company to
issue a Eurobond, which was arranged by the former SG Warburg
and Strauss Turnbull in the mid 1960s.
Previously, Warburg has been involved in the recent
privatisation of British rail infrastructure group Railtrack,
and played a leading role in UK government privatisations
through the 1980s and 1990s.
